title: There is trouble in River City: Gassaway | Opinion | wvnews.com
text:
What started as a season of renewed hope and a vibrant spirit of community well-being in Gassaway has rapidly spiraled into frustration and turmoil. When Paula Cunningham took office as Mayor on July 1, 2025, residents across the town breathed a collective sigh of relief. As a former Braxton County Prosecuting Attorney, it was widely believed that Mayor Cunningham would bring an unprecedented level of seasoned leadership, administrative integrity, and professional rigor to municipal governance. Unfortunately, that hopeful promise has not been realized. Instead of collaborative progress, Gassaway now finds itself mired in political dysfunction, legal uncertainty, and deep internal division.
Rather than fostering an open and efficient local government, the current administration has systematically sidelined our elected city officials. Key processes required by municipal code to run the city have seemingly been cut out entirely. Basic governance standards — such as adhering to Robert’s Rules of Order, properly publishing council agendas, and maintaining a transparent purchase approval process — have fallen by the wayside.
